findings: The run is not an accepted matched performance cohort: each arm independently failed the throughput floor and each arm lost required upstream-origin reuse after an idle age above the fixed 30 second policy.

The four selected diagnostic intervals per arm remain internally valid observational records: sender, raw-write, byte-credit, and server-growth validators accepted them with empty issues and exact conservation.

Across all eight selected intervals, contained raw-write duration accounts for 98.268% to 99.032% of the physical DATA-write envelope duration; this localizes most measured physical-envelope occupancy to the below-TLS raw Write interval, but does not identify kernel wait, delivery time, or the identity of ciphertext produced by a concurrent TLS writer.

Exact byte-zero waits total 0 to 1.741 seconds. Receiver eligibility-to-completion and peer handler-to-notify local sections are microsecond-scale; the clean H2 excess at sequences 9 and 11 is concentrated in waits whose applied ranges include normal_read credit, not forced growth. This excludes the measured post-eligibility local sections and a growth-only explanation, while leaving pre-eligibility consumption cadence and cross-process transit unmeasured.

H1 sequence 14 is a valid same-origin retained revisit and the slowest selected H1 row; its physical envelope is 10.524302218 seconds and contained raw-write occupancy is 10.406462547 seconds. H2 sequence 11 is the slowest selected H2 row and a valid first-post-close visit; its corresponding values are 11.869507314 and 11.754603357 seconds.

H2 sequences 11 and 15 share lane 3, generation 5, stream 6. Sequence 15 has zero byte-zero waits after retained stream history but still records a 7.580787571 second physical envelope and 7.471679040 seconds of contained raw-write occupancy. This separates usable byte credit from below-TLS occupancy without proving which is causal for WAN throughput.

The exact reuse transitions are consistent with the configured 30 second idle expiry: all four 25.089 to 27.628 second revisits retain the origin connection, while all four 30.916 to 31.252 second revisits create a new origin connection and report httptrace idle time zero. No idle-timeout change or runtime fix follows from this result.
limitations: Conditioning failures make cross-arm and phase performance attribution inconclusive; selected records are observational only.
Duration totals from distinct observers are not additive and no cross-process timestamp subtraction is used.
Raw-write activity is temporal occupancy inside the DATA physical envelope, not a call-stack proof that every raw write contains DATA ciphertext.
Raw conn.Write duration includes TLS and TCP/poller effects but does not isolate kernel TCP backpressure, packet delivery, congestion behavior, or peer consumption.
The byte-credit observer begins at receiver eligibility; the interval before eligibility and frame transit to the peer are unmeasured.
Server growth records describe observed current/proposed receive-window state and outcomes; they do not by themselves establish that window growth caused or prevented a sender stall.
Unix timestamps validate only local ordering/containment; monotonic time.Time.Sub-derived duration fields supply segment conservation.
No timestamp arithmetic is performed across endpoints.
Receiver kind normal_read means the non-forced publication path; SYN/ACK flags separately identify initial/open positive updates, so kind alone does not claim consumed-byte recycling.
Positive initial/open updates use the same per-stream relative ordinal and cumulative convention at both endpoints and are included in the exact ordered join.
The interval before receiver eligibility and cross-process frame transit remain unmeasured.
